text:
evan-cs: FYI incoming from a paying customer — embeddings suddenly dropped to 1024 dims after yesterday's deploy. They expect 1536. They see mixed sizes in the same batch. Repro steps below.

sarah-support: ouch. can you paste the minimal repro and request ids? we should triage quickly. :eyes:

ev an-cs: sorry typo — attaching repro here. request ids from customer: rwd_req_9f2a, rwd_req_9f2b. short repro: they call our python SDK with batch of 10 texts, timeout=3s, retries=2. sometimes response vectors are 1536, sometimes 1024.

--- repro (python) ---
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv("REDWOOD_KEY"))
texts = ["t1", "t2", "t3", "t4"]
resp = client.embeddings.create(model="rwd/embed-large", input=texts, batch_size=8, timeout=3, retries=2)
print([len(v) for v in resp.data])
# expected all 1536, observed [1536, 1024, 1536, 1024]

--- end repro ---

liam-sdk: thanks. two quick hypotheses: 1) model alias changed to a different variant (old model=1024, new=1536) and requests racing a rollback/canary could hit either. 2) client-side retry + server-side partial batching caused mixing of vectors from different backend model variants.

liam-sdk: what SDK version is the customer on? we had a retry behavior change in 2.4.0 where retries are per-batch and we don't attach idempotency keys automatically for batch payloads. if they retry the same batch and our backend routed different shards, duplicates/mix can appear.

ev an-cs: customer is on redwood-sdk-python 2.3.1. they said they didnt set any idempotency header.

liam-sdk: ok that aligns. two short mitigations: 1) pin model to an explicit version like "rwd/embed-large@v2" in the request (avoid aliasing). 2) set client retries=0 for now OR add a unique id per input and send it in metadata so we can dedupe server-side. example header: {"Idempotency-Key": "<batch-guid>"} or SDK: client = RedwoodClient(..., retries=0)

liam-sdk: also please ask them to upgrade to sdk 2.4.1 — we added automatic per-batch idempotency keys in that release.

sarah-support: good. can we also confirm if there was a deploy around 1951231000? asking infra to check canary traffic.

deploy-bot: deploy event: service=embed-service, commit=deadbeef, env=prod, started=1951230987, finished=1951231035, rollout-strategy=canary(10%).

liam-sdk: that matches — a canary deploy of a quantized variant with 1024 dim embeddings was rolled to 10% traffic. if some of the customer's batch hit the canary and others hit stable, they'd see mixed dims.

sarah-support: ok next steps: 1) tell customer to pin model version or disable retries (workaround). 2) we'll open an internal incident to revert canary or expand idempotency/validation to reject mismatched-dim responses. 3) ask infra to hold canary until we add a validation gate.

liam-sdk: for immediate customer message, include this snippet to pin a model version:

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"model":"rwd/embed-large@v2","input":["a","b","c"]}'

liam-sdk: and if they prefer sdk patch: client.embeddings.create(model="rwd/embed-large@v2", input=..., retries=0, timeout=10)

sarah-support: wrote back to customer with those workarounds and asked for a short window to fix. customer is ok with temporary disable of retries.

liam-sdk: i'll follow up with runtime to add a server-side response-dim check (reject responses where any vector length != model.expected_dim) and a de-dupe layer keyed by Idempotency-Key.

sarah-support: creating INC ticket #INC-12345 and assigning to eng-runtime. evan, can you paste customer logs and consent to run a targeted traffic replay to repro?

ev an-cs: customer approved. logs attached privately. will add to the ticket. thanks all. :pray:

liam-sdk: quick follow-up note for SRE: until runtime validation is live, be careful with canaries that change response schemas (embedding dims). flagging as high risk.

sarah-support: closing thread after INC created, will update customer when engineering confirms fix. :white_check_mark:
